Pivot the merged time series into wide format (one column per concept)

Source: R/access_core.R
load_merged_ts_wide.Rd

The merged-schema counterpart of fetch_concepts_wide(): reads the pooled ts table built by merge_sources() and pivots it to wide format in SQL, keyed by ehr_id, source_data, src_patient_id, and the requested analysis grain. Use this when you want a cross-source, ehr_id-keyed wide matrix; use fetch_concepts_wide() to pivot a single source's ts_tab before merging.

Usage

load_merged_ts_wide(
  schema,
  spec,
  bin_min = 60,
  analysis_level = c("admission", "icu"),
  window = NULL,
  complete_grid = FALSE,
  n = Inf,
  cohort_only = TRUE,
  clean = c("none", "range"),
  ranges = NULL,
  con = NULL,
  case_adm_only,
  scope_only
)

Arguments

schema

Target schema name passed to merge_sources() (e.g. "rendehr", "trauma_project").

spec

Named list mapping each concept to a character vector of aggregates. Supported: "min", "max", "mean", "median", "sd", "variance", "sum", "n"/"count", "first", and "last"; "all_numeric" expands to all numeric reducers. An unnamed character vector defaults each concept to "mean"; a named character vector is interpreted as concept = aggregate shorthand.

bin_min

Bin width in minutes (default 60). NULL pivots on the raw timestamp. The emitted t_bin column is the 0-based bin index (floor(time / bin_min)), e.g. 0, 1, 2, ... for hourly bins.

analysis_level

"admission" (default) bins on time_since_hadm_min; "icu" bins on time_since_icu_min.

window

Optional c(from_bin, to_bin) in bin-index units, inclusive both ends, restricting the output to those bins (applied in SQL before aggregation). E.g. with bin_min = 60, c(0, 47) keeps the first 48 h, c(0, 0) keeps only the first hour. NULL (default) keeps all bins.

complete_grid

If TRUE, emit a row for every bin in window (or, when window is NULL, the observed bin range) for each stay present in ts, left-joining the aggregates onto the full grid so unmeasured bins come back as NA. No imputation is performed - fill/mask downstream in R. Note this regularizes shape only; it does NOT enforce length-of-stay eligibility, so still filter icu_los from flat to define the cohort. Requires a non-NULL bin_min. Default FALSE.

n

Max rows to return. Default Inf.

cohort_only

If TRUE (default), pivot only rows of cohort members (cohort_index in the merged cohort_info), matched at the requested analysis_level: (source_data, src_admission_id) for "admission", plus assigned_icu_id for "icu" (which needs cohort_info built with analysis_level = "icu"). Applied in SQL before aggregation. FALSE reads all imported context rows; it cannot recover data that was never imported.

clean, ranges

Optional range cleaning before aggregation, as in fetch_concepts_wide(): clean = "range" excludes readings outside the config (or ranges) bounds inside the SQL aggregates, adds a <concept>_n_cleaned column per concept and a clean_report attribute. Default "none".

con

Optional explicit DBI connection.

case_adm_only, scope_only

Removed; supplying either is an error. Use cohort_only.

Value

A wide data frame: ehr_id, source_data, src_patient_id, the merge grain key (src_admission_id, plus assigned_icu_id for ICU-level analysis), the t_bin index column, then one column per concept and aggregate, named <concept>_<aggregate>, or just <concept> when the concept has one aggregate (followed by <concept>_n_cleaned with clean = "range").

Details

Shares the conditional-aggregation engine, binning, per-concept spec, and column-naming rules with fetch_concepts_wide() - see there for details.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
load_merged_ts_wide("rendehr", spec = list(
  hr = c("mean", "max"), sbp = "mean", gcs = "last"
), bin_min = 60)
load_merged_ts_wide("rendehr", spec = list(hr = "mean"), cohort_only = FALSE)

# First 48 h on a complete hourly grid (NA where unmeasured), ICU clock
load_merged_ts_wide("rendehr", spec = list(hr = "last", sbp = "last"),
  bin_min = 60, analysis_level = "icu",
  window = c(0, 47), complete_grid = TRUE)
} # }
